questions.q: Why would you build a dual-axis chart instead of putting two measures on the same single axis?
options: When the two measures are on very different scales, a shared axis makes one of them unreadable — a dual axis gives each measure its own scale while sharing the same category labels
Dual-axis charts always load faster than single-axis charts
A dual-axis chart is only used for maps, never for standard charts
Tableau requires at least two axes for any chart with more than one measure
questions.explain: When measures like Sales (tens of thousands) and Profit Ratio (a small percentage) share one axis, the smaller-scale measure becomes unreadable. A dual axis solves this while still sharing the category axis.

questions.q: How do you turn a second measure on Rows into a dual axis in Tableau?
options: Rename the field to include the word 'axis'
Drag the measure onto the Filters shelf
Change its data type from Continuous to Discrete
Right-click the second measure's pill and select Dual-Axis
questions.explain: Right-clicking the second measure pill on Rows (or Columns) and choosing Dual-Axis layers it onto the same view as a second axis, sharing the same category labels.

questions.q: What turns a dual-axis chart into a true combination chart?
options: Renaming Measure Names to something custom
Giving each axis a different mark type — for example, bars for one measure and a line for the other
Synchronizing the two axes so they share the same scale
Adding a third measure to the view
questions.explain: A dual-axis chart becomes a combination chart once each axis uses a distinct mark type, like Profit as bars and Sales as a line, both sharing the same month labels.

questions.q: What does Synchronize Axis do, and when should you use it?
options: It merges the two measures into a single value
It is required every time you create a dual-axis chart, with no exceptions
It forces both axes to share the same numeric scale — useful when the two measures share the same unit and you want a direct visual comparison of magnitude
It removes one of the two axes entirely
questions.explain: Synchronize Axis aligns the scales of both axes. It's useful when comparing two measures of the same unit directly, but can visually mislead if forced onto measures with genuinely different scales.

questions.q: What field does Tableau automatically add to Color when you convert a second measure into a dual axis?
options: Customer Name
Measure Values
Order Date
Measure Names
questions.explain: Tableau adds Measure Names to Color automatically so the two overlaid measures are visually distinguished by color, as shown in Tableau's own combination-chart documentation.
